Tessa,

- A clear switchover window and rollback plan (we operate in US west) so we can coordinate network changes and DNS cutover.

Would appreciate a short run-of-show and acceptance gates you expect to use.

Felix — thanks for the clear asks. I ran this by Karthik and the infra team and sketched a proposal you can review. Attaching a capacity worksheet and a first-draft migration runbook.

Run-of-show (proposal):
1) Preflight (Day -7 to -3): commit sizing worksheet, confirm model versions and quantization profiles, exchange test replay and credentials.
2) Certification soak (Day 0–2): 72-hour replay against dedicated reservation with production-like client behavior. We will stream logs and SLO dashboards to your team.
3) Acceptance window (Day 3): joint review of latency, error rates, and token/unit economics. If pass, sign-off for switchover.
4) Switchover (Day 4): planned 2‑hour swap window (DNS + routing) with a 60‑minute monitoring hold and immediate rollback plan if critical regressions.

Acceptance gates we propose:
- 95/99/99.9 latency within agreed baselines (we'll produce p50/p90/p99 traces)
- <0.5% error budget consumption vs hosted baseline
- Throughput within ±10% of expected tokens/sec during peak replay windows

Preliminary dates: if you want May 24–28 for the certification soak, we can target May 24 start (preflight completes by May 20). If you need it earlier we have limited earlier slots May 18–20 but would need fast turnaround on the worksheet.

Attachments: capacity-cert-sheet.xlsx, migration-runbook-v1.md

Karthik — can you confirm the GPU mix (SKU list) and the tests we'll run for KV cache warmup and prefix caching?

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Tessa@redwood.com

Hi all — quick technical confirmation and the tests we'll execute during the 72h soak.

Committed fleet (proposed):
- 8x A800 80GB (in 4x pairs with NVLink) for generating top‑k variants
- 4x A800 40GB for lower-memory models and embedding workloads
- 1x control headnode for routing and KV cache persistence

Rationales: the 8x 80GB covers your peak concurrent streams with room for auto-bursting; the 40GB machines cover embedding-heavy backends you mentioned. If you have strict isolation needs we can convert one 80GB pair to dedicated-only—flag if required.

Validation plan (tests we'll run):
- Startup: model load latency verification (cold start) per SKU, sequential 10 runs, median and 95th.
- Throughput sweep: replay traffic at 50/75/100/125% of expected peak to validate linearity and tail behavior.
- KV / prefix cache warmup: run scripted prefix warmers (your replay plus synthetic hot prefixes) and measure hit-rate and token reduction.
- Stability soak: 72h continuous run with error/latency tracking, resource and thermals monitoring (OOM, GPU ECC).
- Failover exercise: induce a graceful node restart and validate routing fallback to secondary nodes (no more than 2% error spike allowed).

Metrics we'll stream to you: Prometheus endpoint + Grafana dashboard, token/sec, per-model p50/p90/p99, errors per minute, GPU util / mem / temp, and KV hit ratio. We'll share dashboard links during preflight.

Smoke test (pre‑cutover): a short 30‑minute targeted replay that exercises auth, routing, and one critical model path — this is non-negotiable before DNS swap. See attached smoke-test-checklist.pdf.

If all good, tech approves May 24–27 soak; please confirm replay handoff and who on your side will run the replay.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
